post:
A client called at 10 PM, furious.

His employee had just been stopped at Muscat airport. Overstayed visa. Deportation flag.

The renewal was on the Sanad manager's list. Somewhere between a WhatsApp message from three weeks ago and a tab on a shared Excel file nobody had updated.

That call ended a two-year client relationship.

If you run a Sanad office in Oman, you know exactly how that happens. Not because anyone is careless — but because you are managing 40 work permits, 15 visa renewals, and 8 MOL filings across 20 client companies using tools that were never built for this.

WhatsApp is not a compliance system. Excel is not a document vault. And a handwritten register won't alert you 30 days before a visa expires.

924 licensed Sanad offices operate across Oman. Every one of them is the legal gateway for their clients' government paperwork. The risk surface is enormous. The tools most are using are not.
